title: Tower-flora foundational growth architecture
scope: Foundational growth architecture of the K2 tower-flora kingdom at qualitative strategy grain; usable within shared-setting ecology and adopted downstream story development.
claims: Tower flora are individual, non-networked organisms; root contact between towers is ordinary competition or incidental interaction, not kingdom-defining resource sharing.
A tower grows from a single persistent living core column.
Each growth season the core lays down an external structural casing layer that then dies, so a mature tower is a living column sheathed in successive dead, self-supporting casings.

Because living tissue lies deep, surface damage, scorching, and girdling-equivalent injuries are survivable in principle, while damage or decay reaching the living core is the characteristic mortal wound.
Towers are long-lived and slow to replace; loss of mature towers is a lasting landscape change.
Seasonal growth is strongly pulsed, compatible with the established climate and pulse-mosaic ecology.
Reproduction concentrates in episodic heavy seeding years rather than uniform annual output.
boundaries: Tower, core, casing, and seeding year are author-facing functional descriptions, not in-world names or formal taxonomy.
The architecture establishes no Earth wood, bark, growth-ring, heartwood, cambium, or tree homology.
Species, branch structure, dimensions, proportions, lifespan, growth rates, and silhouettes beyond the theme remain open.
Core and casing anatomy, chemistry, material properties, strength, decay, flammability, and insulation remain open.

Survivable surface damage is a structural tendency, not invulnerability; no tolerance threshold, healing rate, or fire immunity is established, and crown or root damage, drought, disease, and pests can still kill without a core breach.
Possible kill-free casing removal is a structural implication only; no harvest practice, tool, yield, or human use is established.
Energy capture, leaf-analogue structures, root form, water handling, and winter state remain open.
Seeding mechanisms, structures, dispersal, edibility, period, synchrony scale, and triggers remain open; episodic seeding establishes no fixed cycle or guaranteed mast.
No kingdom assignment is made for the western temperate rainforest, basin woodland, or any other named vegetation; K2 remains only their candidate home.
No tower-flora member is established as present, dominant, or absent at any particular location.
Pests, diseases, decomposition, and symbioses, including any partnership with K6 thread decomposers, remain open.
Earth and mythological inspiration remains author-facing; no living, extinct, or legendary Earth species is transplanted.

Mana patterns remain open; no Mana organ, specialised ability, System progression, spawn point, refill node, guaranteed harvest, reward, Skill, trait payload, or Ancestry Development rule is established.
Water, energy, nutrients, space, growth time, disturbance, disease, and decay remain binding ecological constraints.
story_implications: Woodland scenes can show layered dead casings around living cores, scorched-but-living towers, and core-rot stakes.
Mast-year abundance gives later food-web and forage records a pulse mechanism to develop.
Future timber-analogue, fire, disease, and harvest development gains grounded, boundable hooks.
Every species, local presence, practice, and event requires its own evidence and records.
system_implications: The architecture describes ordinary planetary ecology under CAL0 WLD1.2D and WLD2.1A+D.
No System mechanic, guaranteed harvest, spawn source, refill node, reward, or specialised Mana ability is established.
research_questions: What core and casing anatomy, chemistry, and material properties implement the architecture?
What energy capture, leaf-analogue, and root strategies do tower-flora branches use?
How do seeding years work: structures, dispersal, synchrony, triggers, and edibility?
Do the western rainforest and basin woodland belong to K2, and through which member guilds?
Which pests, diseases, and K6 partnerships shape tower life and death?
Which casing properties would support later material-culture development?

author_approval.evidence: After the A/B/C architecture cards were presented with A recommended, the Author selected 'A — Core-and-casing' on 2026-08-17.
